The core insight of the proposal lies in the interplay between asynchronous data streams and robust statistical inference. Theorem 4 introduces a mathematical framework where rough path theory ensures that even when data arrives at irregular intervals—such as nurse charting rates changing—the inferred properties remain stable. This is achieved by embedding the signal into a higher-order signature space, which captures all relevant path information up to a certain level. The log-signature then acts as an invariant representation under reparametrization, thus providing immunity against confounding introduced by sampling rate variations. The integration of this with doubly-adaptive conformal risk control allows for dynamic adjustment of prediction intervals while maintaining theoretical guarantees on coverage. Meanwhile, the surrogate axonal waveguide provides a physical model linking abstract signal processing to real-world neurobiological phenomena, grounding the abstraction in measurable physiological responses. Together, these primitives form a coherent architecture capable of handling both temporal variability and structural complexity in clinical settings.
